title: Private Hire Driver Licence Knowledge Test

bank.question: How long is a standard TfL private hire driver's licence usually valid for?
bank.explanation: TfL grants standard PHV driver licences for a three-year period subject to checks
options: 1 Year
3 Years
5 Years
10 Years

bank.question: A driver may be prosecuted for 'Assisting an Offender' if they knowingly transport a passenger who is in possession of illegal drugs
bank.explanation: If you are aware that a passenger is carrying drugs or planning a crime, allowing the journey to continue could lead to charges of conspiracy or aiding and abetting

bank.question: A licensed Private Hire driver is allowed to pick up passengers who wave them down in the street
bank.explanation: Private Hire vehicles cannot be hailed in the street or wait at taxi ranks; they must be pre-booked through a licensed operator

bank.question: A person approaches your car and asks if you are free to take them home. How should you respond?
bank.explanation: Private hire drivers cannot accept fares directly; all bookings must be processed by a licensed operator before the journey starts
options: Negotiate a cash price and start the journey immediately
Politely refuse and ask the passenger to book through your licensed operator
Accept the fare as long as you use the meter
Tell them to get in and you will call the office halfway through the trip

bank.question: Which of the following are mandatory responsibilities of a licensed Private Hire Driver? (Select 3)
bank.explanation: PHV drivers must carry their ID badge at all times, follow Highway Code rules, and ensure the vehicle is clean and safe. Meter updates are only required for specific council-regulated tariffs. The correct answers are Wearing their photographic ID badge at all times while working, Following all rules set out in the Highway Code and Ensuring the vehicle is kept in a clean and roadworthy condition.
options: Wearing their photographic ID badge at all times while working
Charging passengers double the fare if they are rude
Following all rules set out in the Highway Code
Ensuring the vehicle is kept in a clean and roadworthy condition

bank.question: The licensing authority does not require drivers to have any basic understanding of the English language as long as they have a valid UK driving licence
bank.explanation: Licensing rules generally require that all drivers have a functional understanding of English to communicate with passengers and emergency services

bank.question: Before working as a London PHV driver, you must be licensed by
bank.explanation: Transport for London is the licensing authority for taxi and private hire in the capital
options: Your local council
TfL
DVSA
The Met Police

bank.question: What does the law state regarding carrying assistance dogs in a Private Hire Vehicle?
bank.explanation: Assistance dogs (like Guide Dogs) must be carried by law unless the driver has a valid medical exemption certificate issued by the licensing authority
options: You can charge double the fare for cleaning costs
The dog must be placed in a crate in the boot
You can refuse any passenger with an animal
You must carry the dog at no extra cost unless you have a medical exemption certificate

bank.question: If a passenger leaves property in your vehicle, you must report it according to your licensing authority's guidelines
bank.explanation: If you find an item of value, you are legally required to report it or take it to a police station or your operator's designated lost property office

bank.question: It is the driver's responsibility to ensure they do not drive while tired, even if they have not yet reached their maximum hours for the day
bank.explanation: Fatigue is a major cause of road accidents; the licensing authority expects drivers to manage their hours to ensure they are fit to drive

bank.question: Which of the following driving actions are generally prohibited for PHV drivers? (Select 2)
bank.explanation: Private Hire Vehicles cannot use bus lanes unless specific local signage permits it, and they must never pick up unbooked passengers or park on zig-zag lines. The correct answers are Stopping at a designated rank only if it is for PHVs (not 'Taxis only') and Complying with 'No Waiting' restrictions on red routes.
options: Picking up a passenger who hails you on the street
Stopping at a designated rank only if it is for PHVs (not 'Taxis only')
Complying with 'No Waiting' restrictions on red routes
Using a bus lane at any time of day regardless of signage

bank.question: Is it ever acceptable to stop or park on yellow zig-zag lines outside a school?
bank.explanation: Parking on zig-zag lines, especially near schools or crossings, is a safety hazard and is strictly prohibited at all times
options: It is strictly prohibited and a safety hazard
Only if the driver stays in the vehicle with the engine running
Only to pick up or drop off school children
It is allowed for up to two minutes

bank.question: Private hire bookings in London must always be
bank.explanation: Only licensed black cabs may be hailed or use ranks; PHVs must be pre-booked via a licensed operator
options: Pre-booked through a licensed operator
Hailed in the street
Picked up at a rank
Arranged by phone only

bank.question: You must wear or display your driver's badge in a way that is clearly visible to passengers at all times when working
bank.explanation: This is a standard requirement for private hire drivers to ensure they are easily identifiable to passengers and enforcement officers

bank.question: It is a criminal offence to refuse a passenger because they are accompanied by a guide dog
bank.explanation: Under the Equality Act 2010, it is illegal to refuse a passenger because they have an assistance dog, unless the driver has a medical exemption certificate

bank.question: What should you do if you arrive at a pickup location and the passenger is not there?
bank.explanation: A 'no-show' occurs if the passenger isn't there. You should wait a reasonable time and contact your operator for instructions before moving on
options: Immediately drive away and cancel the booking
Wait at the pickup point and contact your operator for further instructions
Get out of the car and knock on every door in the street
Pick up a different person standing on the street instead

bank.question: What are the correct procedures for safeguarding vulnerable passengers? (Select 3)
bank.explanation: When dealing with vulnerable adults or children, you should report concerns to the police/operator, keep doors unlocked for their safety, and stay in the vehicle unless assisting. The correct answers are Reporting any concerns about a passenger's safety to your operator, Keeping the vehicle doors unlocked so the passenger does not feel trapped and Allowing the passenger to sit in the rear of the vehicle.
options: Reporting any concerns about a passenger's safety to your operator
Keeping the vehicle doors unlocked so the passenger does not feel trapped
Initiating personal conversations about their private life
Allowing the passenger to sit in the rear of the vehicle

bank.question: It is legal to use an e-cigarette (vape) inside your licensed vehicle as long as there are no passengers present
bank.explanation: UK law prohibits smoking or vaping in all enclosed workplaces and public spaces, including licensed vehicles, even when empty

bank.question: Which document must be displayed inside a licensed private hire vehicle?
bank.explanation: Both the driver and vehicle identifiers issued by TfL must be displayed
options: Driver's CV
TfL driver and vehicle ID disc
V5C
MOT certificate

bank.question: What should you do if you suspect a passenger is a victim of human trafficking or being exploited?
bank.explanation: Drivers should be aware of signs of modern slavery or exploitation, such as passengers being directed by others or appearing frightened and confused
options: Wait and see if they become more comfortable during the trip
Ignore it, as it is not the driver's business
Report your concerns to the police or your operator's safeguarding lead
Ask the passenger directly if they are being trafficked

bank.question: Private Hire drivers are permitted to exceed the speed limit if a passenger is in danger of missing a flight
bank.explanation: PHV drivers must adhere to the same speed limits as all other road users, regardless of whether a passenger is in a hurry

bank.question: If you are diagnosed with a new medical condition that could affect your driving, you must inform the licensing authority immediately
bank.explanation: Public safety is paramount; any condition that affects your ability to drive must be reported and may require a medical assessment

bank.question: Which of the following are requirements for a booking to be considered legal? (Select 2)
bank.explanation: A booking is only legal if it is recorded by the licensed operator before the journey begins; drivers cannot accept bookings directly. The correct answers are Ensuring the booking has been confirmed by your licensed operator first and Receiving booking details via the operator's app or radio system.
options: Accepting a cash booking directly from a regular customer via your personal phone
Ensuring the booking has been confirmed by your licensed operator first
Receiving booking details via the operator's app or radio system
Picking up a friend who asks for a lift for money without a booking

bank.question: If you develop a medical condition that may affect your driving, what is your legal obligation?
bank.explanation: The licensing authority requires drivers to be 'fit and proper,' which includes reporting medical conditions that might impact driving safety
options: Registering the condition with the licensing authority and the DVLA
Keeping it secret to avoid losing your licence
Taking extra caffeine to stay alert while driving
Only telling your insurance company

bank.question: The minimum age to apply for a TfL PHV driver's licence is
bank.explanation: Applicants must usually be at least 21 and have held a full DVLA licence for three years

bank.question: A Private Hire driver can pick up a passenger who approaches them in a supermarket car park asking for a lift, as long as they agree on a price first
bank.explanation: PHV drivers are only permitted to pick up passengers who have pre-booked their journey through a licensed operator

bank.question: You must notify the licensing authority in writing if you receive a motoring conviction or fixed penalty notice
bank.explanation: Licensing authorities require drivers to disclose any new convictions or fixed penalties within a specific timeframe (usually 7 days)

bank.question: Who is legally responsible for ensuring a child under 14 wears a seatbelt or correct restraint in a PHV?
bank.explanation: Seatbelts save lives. Drivers are responsible for ensuring all passengers under 14 use the correct restraints. Adults are responsible for themselves
options: The police officer who stops the car
The passenger's parents, even if they aren't in the car
The passenger themselves
The driver of the vehicle

bank.question: What are the legal requirements regarding assistance dogs in PHVs? (Select 2)
bank.explanation: Assistance dogs must be carried for free unless the driver has a medical exemption certificate issued by the licensing authority. The correct answers are The dog must be allowed to sit with the passenger and The driver must carry the dog unless they have a valid medical exemption certificate.
options: The dog must be allowed to sit with the passenger
The driver can charge an extra GBP 5 for cleaning after the dog
The driver must carry the dog unless they have a valid medical exemption certificate
The dog must always be kept in the boot of the vehicle

bank.question: The minimum legal tread depth for tyres on a licensed private hire vehicle is 1.0mm
bank.explanation: By law, the minimum legal tread depth for car tyres in the UK is 1.6mm across the central three-quarters of the breadth

bank.question: If your driving licence is endorsed during your PHV licence period, you must
bank.explanation: Drivers must notify TfL of relevant changes including endorsements
options: Ignore it
Notify TfL within the required period
Tell only your operator
Wait until renewal

bank.question: What is the minimum legal tread depth for tyres on a Private Hire Vehicle in the UK?
bank.explanation: Tyre tread depth must be at least 1.6mm across the central three-quarters of the tyre and around the entire circumference
options: 1.0Mm
2.5Mm village standard
1.6Mm
3.0Mm

bank.question: A child under the age of 12 does not count as a passenger when calculating the vehicle's maximum seating capacity
bank.explanation: Even if a child is under 12, they count as one person towards the vehicle's total seating capacity as listed on the licence

bank.question: A licensed operator can legally pass a booking to another licensed operator if they are unable to fulfill the journey themselves
bank.explanation: Operators may use subcontractors to fulfil bookings, but they must ensure the subcontracted firm and driver are also properly licensed

bank.question: What steps should a driver take if a passenger leaves property in the vehicle? (Select 3)
bank.explanation: If you find property, you should check the car immediately, record the item, and report it to your operator or the police as per local policy. The correct answers are Checking the vehicle for lost property after every single journey, Recording details of the item and the journey it was found on and Reporting the lost property to your operator or base as soon as possible.
options: Checking the vehicle for lost property after every single journey
Recording details of the item and the journey it was found on
Keeping the item for your own use if it is not claimed within 24 hours
Reporting the lost property to your operator or base as soon as possible

bank.question: Where should a satellite navigation (sat-nav) device be positioned in the vehicle?
bank.explanation: Using a sat-nav is helpful, but the screen must be positioned so it does not obscure the driver's view of the road
options: In the centre of the steering wheel
In a position that does not block your view of the road or mirrors
Attached to the side window next to your face
It doesn't matter where it is as long as you can see it clearly

bank.question: Operating as a PHV driver without a valid licence is
bank.explanation: Driving an unlicensed PHV is a criminal offence under the Private Hire Vehicles (London) Act 1998
options: A civil matter
A criminal offence
A minor warning
Allowed once

bank.question: It is a criminal offence for a private hire driver to refuse to carry a passenger solely because they are accompanied by a guide dog
bank.explanation: The Equality Act 2010 makes it illegal to refuse an assistance dog unless the driver has a valid medical exemption certificate

bank.question: A Private Hire driver must wear or clearly display their ID badge while they are available for work
bank.explanation: To maintain safety standards, you must carry your photographic driver's ID badge at all times while working

bank.question: How must a Private Hire Driver's licence badge be worn or displayed?
bank.explanation: The licence badge must be clearly visible so passengers can verify that both the driver and the vehicle are properly licensed
options: Worn on your person or displayed in a way that is clearly visible to passengers
Kept inside your wallet or glove box for safety
Left at the operator's base while you are working
Kept at home to ensure it isn't lost or stolen

bank.question: Which of the following are part of a driver's daily vehicle safety checks? (Select 2)
bank.explanation: Checking tyres and lights are daily maintenance tasks; MOTs and licensing updates are periodic legal requirements. The correct answers are Checking tyre pressure and tread depth every day and Ensuring all interior and exterior lights are clean and functioning.
options: Checking tyre pressure and tread depth every day
Waiting for the annual MOT to check if the headlamps work
Ensuring all interior and exterior lights are clean and functioning
Ignoring a dashboard warning light if the car still feels fine to drive

bank.question: If your vehicle licence expires, you can still carry out pre-booked work for 48 hours while you wait for your renewal to be processed
bank.explanation: An operator is not permitted to accept a booking if the vehicle or driver being used is currently suspended or unlicensed

bank.question: PHV drivers must hold what type of insurance?
bank.explanation: Hire and reward cover is required for any vehicle carrying paying passengers
options: Social, domestic and pleasure
Hire and reward
Third-party only
None

bank.question: What are the consequences if a PHV driver accepts a fare that has not been pre-booked through their operator?
bank.explanation: A Private Hire Vehicle must be pre-booked through a licensed operator; plying for hire (picking up unbooked passengers) is illegal and invalidates your insurance
options: It is legal if the journey is less than two miles
It is legal as long as you charge a flat cash rate
It is illegal and your insurance will be invalid
It is allowed if the passenger has the operator's app

bank.question: If a PHV driver accepts a fare without a booking, their hire and reward insurance remains fully valid
bank.explanation: Plying for hire (picking up unbooked fares) is illegal for PHV drivers and can void your insurance policy entirely

bank.question: A driver should provide reasonable assistance with a passenger's luggage, such as loading it into the boot
bank.explanation: Drivers are expected to assist passengers with luggage to provide good customer service, provided it is safe and they are physically able

bank.question: Which behaviors are associated with professional and safe driving? (Select 2)
bank.explanation: Aggressive driving and speeding increase the risk of collisions and reduce passenger comfort. Correcting others' driving is not the driver's role. The correct answers are Maintaining a safe following distance from the vehicle in front and Staying calm and patient even if other road users are being difficult.
options: Speeding only when the passenger says they are in a hurry
Maintaining a safe following distance from the vehicle in front
Braking and accelerating harshly to save time between jobs
Staying calm and patient even if other road users are being difficult

bank.question: Under UK law, when is a licensed PHV driver exempt from the requirement to wear a seatbelt?
bank.explanation: Private Hire Drivers are generally exempt from wearing seatbelts only when they are actively carrying a passenger for hire
options: Only when they are carrying a passenger for hire
At all times while driving the vehicle
Only when driving during daylight hours
Only when the vehicle is traveling under 30mph

bank.question: What is the maximum number of passengers you are allowed to carry in your private hire vehicle?
bank.explanation: A private hire vehicle can only carry the maximum number of passengers specified on its vehicle licence plate
options: As many people as can fit safely
Any number as long as everyone wears a seatbelt
The maximum number shown on the vehicle licence plate
One person for every window in the car

bank.question: A passenger does not have the right to know the estimated cost of a journey before the trip begins
bank.explanation: A driver/operator must provide a clear estimate or explain how the fare is calculated (e.g., via a meter or set rate) when the booking is made

bank.question: It is the driver's legal responsibility to ensure that passengers under 14 years old wear a seatbelt
bank.explanation: The driver is legally responsible for ensuring any child under the age of 14 uses a seatbelt or the correct child restraint

bank.question: If a passenger requests a specific route that is different from your sat-nav, what should you do?
bank.explanation: While you can suggest a route, the passenger technically pays for the service and has the right to choose the specific route taken
options: The driver must always use the route provided by the sat-nav
The driver should follow the passenger's preferred route
The driver must take the most expensive route possible
The driver should ignore the passenger and take the quickest way

bank.question: Which of the following are legal requirements for a PHV journey to take place? (Select 3)
bank.explanation: The PHV licence must be displayed, the car must have valid hire and reward insurance, and the driver must wear their ID badge. Private vehicles do not need a meter unless required by the operator. The correct answers are The vehicle must display valid PHV licence plates or discs, The driver must have 'Hire and Reward' insurance in place and The driver must visibly wear their official licensing badge.
options: The vehicle must display valid PHV licence plates or discs
The driver must have 'Hire and Reward' insurance in place
The driver must visibly wear their official licensing badge
The vehicle must have a roof sign that says 'TAXI'

bank.question: If you are involved in a road traffic accident that damages your licensed vehicle, you must report the incident to the licensing authority
bank.explanation: Drivers must report all road traffic accidents that cause damage to their vehicle to the licensing authority, usually within 72 hours

bank.question: If a passenger has an assistance dog, how much extra are you allowed to charge them for the journey?
bank.explanation: The Equality Act 2010 makes it illegal to refuse or charge extra for a passenger with an assistance dog
options: You cannot charge any extra for carrying an assistance dog
You can charge a small cleaning fee up front
You can charge 50% extra on the total fare
You can charge a flat rate of GBP 5 extra

bank.question: What is the primary risk of adopting an aggressive driving style, such as tailgating or rapid acceleration?
bank.explanation: Aggressive driving (tailgating, speeding) increases the risk of accidents and creates a high-stress environment for both driver and passenger
options: It improves fuel efficiency
It helps the driver finish their shift faster
It is a requirement for meeting booking deadlines
It increases the risk of collisions and causes passenger discomfort

bank.question: Drivers are allowed to smoke or vape inside the licensed vehicle as long as no passengers are present
bank.explanation: Smoking (including the use of e-cigarettes) is strictly prohibited in any licensed PHV at all times, even without passengers

bank.question: You may display a 'For Hire' sign in the windscreen of your private hire vehicle when you are not currently on a booking
bank.explanation: Displaying unauthorised signs or 'For Hire' lights can lead to prosecution for plying for hire and may violate licensing conditions

bank.question: How should a driver handle a conflict with a passenger? (Select 2)
bank.explanation: Aggressive behavior or direct physical contact is never appropriate; use the operator for support or the police in emergencies. The correct answers are Remaining professional and polite at all times and Contacting your operator for advice if a passenger becomes difficult.
options: Remaining professional and polite at all times
Using physical force to remove a passenger who refuses to pay
Contacting your operator for advice if a passenger becomes difficult
Shouting back at a passenger to show you are in charge

bank.question: If you are involved in a collision and your passenger appears to be injured, what should you do?
bank.explanation: A driver should never attempt to move a passenger who appears injured; instead, call 999 and follow the operator's instructions
options: Move them out of the car and onto the pavement immediately
Keep them calm, do not move them, and call emergency services
Drive them to the nearest hospital as fast as possible
Give them water and ask them to walk around to check for pain

bank.question: Within how many days must you notify the licensing authority if you change your home address?
bank.explanation: If you change your home address, you must notify the licensing authority (e.g., TfL) in writing within 21 days
options: Immediately before you move
Within 21 days of the change occurring
Only when you renew your licence
Within 60 days of the change occurring

bank.question: If a passenger is travelling with a child under 3 years old and they do not have a child car seat, you must refuse the journey
bank.explanation: A child under 3 may travel without a seatbelt in the rear of a licensed private hire vehicle if a correct child seat is not available

bank.question: Private Hire vehicles are not always permitted to use bus lanes; you must check the signs for the 'PHV' or 'Taxi' symbol
bank.explanation: In some areas, PHVs are prohibited from certain lanes; however, in most of London and other UK cities, specific signage dictates access

bank.question: Is a driver permitted to smoke an electronic cigarette (vape) inside their licensed PHV when they are not carrying a passenger?
bank.explanation: A PHV is a smoke-free zone at all times, including when the driver is off-duty and no passengers are present
options: No, it is illegal to smoke in a licensed vehicle at any time
Yes, but only if the windows are fully open
Yes, but only if the driver is not working
Yes, but only if the driver uses an electronic cigarette

bank.question: When transporting a passenger with a physical disability, what are your duties? (Select 3)
bank.explanation: Drivers have a duty to assist disabled passengers, ensure wheelchairs are secured, and must not charge extra for the assistance. The correct answers are Helping the passenger get in and out of the vehicle if requested, Ensuring a wheelchair is safely secured using the correct equipment and Being patient and allowing the passenger extra time to settle.
options: Helping the passenger get in and out of the vehicle if requested
Ensuring a wheelchair is safely secured using the correct equipment
Charging a 'convenience fee' for the time taken to load a wheelchair
Being patient and allowing the passenger extra time to settle

bank.question: A licensed driver is legally exempt from wearing a seatbelt while they are actively transporting a passenger
bank.explanation: Private Hire drivers are exempt from wearing seatbelts only when they are actively carrying a fare-paying passenger

bank.question: Which of the following is a private hire driver legally allowed to do?
bank.explanation: A private hire driver can only accept bookings made through a licensed private hire operator; street hailing is illegal for PHVs
options: Wait at a taxi rank
Pick up a passenger who hails you in the street
Accept a booking directly from a passenger via their phone number
Accept a booking passed to you by a licensed operator

bank.question: How should a PHV driver calculate the fare for a passenger who uses a wheelchair?
bank.explanation: Under the Equality Act 2010, drivers must not charge extra for carrying passengers with disabilities or their assistance dogs
options: Charging 50% extra for the additional time taken
Charging a flat 'cleaning fee' for assistance dogs
Charging the same fare as they would for any other passenger
Setting a higher minimum fare for wheelchair users

bank.question: A Private Hire driver can work for an unlicensed operator as long as the driver's own licence is valid
bank.explanation: A driver can only work for a licensed operator located within the district where the driver's licence was issued

bank.question: If your insurance policy covers 'Hire and Reward', you are legally allowed to pick up passengers who flag you down on the street
bank.explanation: Plying for hire (picking up unbooked passengers) is a criminal offence and usually invalidates your hire and reward insurance

bank.question: Which changes must you report to the Licensing Authority? (Select 2)
bank.explanation: Licensing authorities require notification of any change in health or address to ensure records are accurate and the driver remains fit to work. The correct answers are Being diagnosed with a new medical condition like diabetes or heart issues and Changing your home address or contact phone number.
options: A change of your home's interior paint colour
Being diagnosed with a new medical condition like diabetes or heart issues
Changing your home address or contact phone number
Buying a new set of personal clothes for work

bank.question: What does a double red line at the side of the road signify for a PHV driver?
bank.explanation: Double red lines indicate a 'Red Route' where stopping is strictly prohibited at all times to keep traffic moving
options: You can stop for up to 2 minutes to drop off
You must not stop at any time, even to drop off or pick up
You can stop only if you keep your hazard lights on
You can stop if you have a blue badge displayed

bank.question: If you are transporting a child or a vulnerable adult, what should you do if you need to leave the car to run an errand?
bank.explanation: Drivers should never leave children or vulnerable adults alone in the vehicle, even for a short period
options: Lock the doors and run the errand quickly
Leave the keys in the ignition so they have air conditioning
Never leave them alone in the vehicle for any reason
Ask a nearby member of the public to watch them

bank.question: A licensed operator is required by law to keep records of every booking made through their firm
bank.explanation: Operators must keep a record of every booking, including the pick-up point, destination, and the driver/vehicle used

bank.question: If you move house, you only need to tell your insurance company and not the licensing authority
bank.explanation: A private hire driver must notify the licensing authority of any change of address, usually within seven days, to keep their records and licence valid

bank.question: What should you do if you start to feel sleepy while you are driving a passenger to their destination?
bank.explanation: Being tired significantly slows your reactions and impairs judgement, making you as dangerous as a drunk driver
options: Open the window for fresh air and continue
Drink a high-caffeine energy drink and keep driving
Turn up the radio volume to stay alert
Stop in a safe place, notify your operator, and take a break

bank.question: Which of the following personal changes MUST you report to the Licensing Authority? (Select 3)
bank.explanation: PHV drivers must inform the authority of any medical condition that affects driving, any new driving endorsements, and any change of home address. The correct answers are Change of home address, New points on your driving licence and Developing a heart condition.
options: Change of home address
Joining a new gym
New points on your driving licence
Developing a heart condition

bank.question: You only need to inform the licensing authority about a criminal conviction once you have been found guilty in court
bank.explanation: If you are charged with a recordable offence, you must notify the licensing authority in writing within the timeframe specified in your policy (often 7 days)

bank.question: Where must the official PHV licence discs be displayed on a licensed vehicle?
bank.explanation: The PHV licence disc must be clearly visible to the public and not obscured by any other items or stickers
options: On the front and rear windscreens as specified by the authority
In the glove compartment for safekeeping
Only on the rear bumper next to the number plate
Under the driver's seat

bank.question: Where must the vehicle licence discs be displayed on a licensed Private Hire Vehicle?
bank.explanation: The PHV licence disc must be clearly visible to the public and authorities to prove the vehicle is legally licensed
options: It must be clearly displayed on the front and rear windscreens as required
It should be kept in the glove box to keep it clean
It only needs to be shown if a police officer asks for it
It must be stuck to the driver's sun visor

bank.question: A driver should check their vehicle for any items left behind by passengers at the end of every journey
bank.explanation: It is common practice and often a licensing requirement for drivers to check for lost property as soon as a passenger leaves the vehicle

bank.question: It is a licensing breach for a private hire vehicle to pull up and wait on a designated taxi rank
bank.explanation: Private hire vehicles must be pre-booked through a licensed operator; they cannot use taxi ranks, which are for Hackney Carriages only

bank.question: Which of the following are legal ways for a PHV driver to pick up passengers? (Select 2)
bank.explanation: PHVs can only take passengers who have booked in advance through a licensed operator; they cannot be hailed or use taxi ranks. The correct answers are Picking up a passenger from a pre-booked airport transfer and Picking up a passenger from a pre-booked wedding venue.
options: Picking up a passenger who hails you in the street
Picking up a passenger from a pre-booked airport transfer
Waiting on a public rank for your next job
Picking up a passenger from a pre-booked wedding venue

bank.question: Your vehicle is licensed to carry 4 passengers. A group of 5 people (3 adults and 2 children) asks for a lift. What should you do?
bank.explanation: Overloading a vehicle is illegal and dangerous; you must never exceed the number of passengers specified on the vehicle licence
options: Allow it, as long as the children sit on the adults' laps
Allow it if the journey is very short
Politely refuse and explain that your insurance only covers 4 passengers
Ask for an extra payment to cover the additional risk

bank.question: When are you required to give a passenger a receipt for their journey?
bank.explanation: Drivers must provide a receipt if requested, which should include the fare, date, and driver's details
options: Only if the fare is over GBP 20
If the passenger asks for one
Only if the passenger paid by credit card
It is never required for private hire journeys

bank.question: You are permitted to smoke inside your licensed vehicle as long as you are not working and the 'No Smoking' signs are removed
bank.explanation: All licensed vehicles are strictly smoke-free by law at all times, even when the driver is off-duty or alone in the car

bank.question: A driver can take a booking directly from a customer using their personal mobile phone without involving the operator
bank.explanation: All bookings must be made through a licensed Private Hire Operator; drivers cannot take bookings directly from customers

bank.question: Which of the following is the most important safety precaution to take before reversing your vehicle?
bank.explanation: Checking the area behind the vehicle is vital before reversing to ensure no children, pedestrians, or small obstacles are in the blind spot
options: Rely solely on your wing mirrors
Check all around the vehicle, especially the blind spot behind you
Beep your horn twice before moving
Put your hazard lights on and reverse quickly

bank.question: Which actions demonstrate high standards of customer service? (Select 3)
bank.explanation: Good service includes checking the temperature, asking if the route is okay, and helping with luggage to ensure passenger comfort. The correct answers are Offering to help with heavy shopping or suitcases, Asking the passenger if the air conditioning level is comfortable and Confirming the destination and preferred route before starting.
options: Offering to help with heavy shopping or suitcases
Asking the passenger if the air conditioning level is comfortable
Confirming the destination and preferred route before starting
Asking the passenger for their personal phone number

bank.question: A driver is legally entitled to choose a longer route to avoid traffic without informing the passenger, as long as they arrive safely
